shortDescription: Canada's main stock index advanced more than 1% on Wednesday as Democrats swept the US midterm elections, with higher gold prices boosting mining shares.The S&P/TSX Composite Index TSX:TSX was up 1.29% at 35,990.05 points as of 1036 a.m. ET (1536 GMT).

children: Canada's main stock index advanced more than 1% on Wednesday as Democrats swept the US midterm elections, with higher gold prices boosting mining shares.
was up 1.29% at 35,990.05 points as of 1036 a.m. ET (1536 GMT).

Democrats seized control of both chambers of the US Congress on Tuesday, scoring sweeping victories in Republican strongholds — including border states like Minnesota, Maine and Michigan — and delivering a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump

"There's definitely a signal that several Republican-held seats along the border flipped to Democrats, as those states appear to be feeling the impact of the trade war with Canada, said Greg Taylor, chief investment officer at PenderFund Capital Management
That could push Washington to ease its position, Taylor said, with some tariffs potentially rolled back and a deal reached in the near term
became the biggest gainer in the index, advancing 5%, as gold prices rose in the wake of the election results
Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) rose 1.9%, while consumer discretionary stocks (.GSPTTCD) also climbed 3.1%
was the biggest loser, declining about 4%, as Brent crude
fell below $100 a barrel for the first time since October 7
Investors are now awaiting Washington's next move in the US-Israeli war on Iran
Meanwhile, Canada's employment report is due on Friday, with economists polled by Reuters expecting the economy to have added 13,600 jobs last month while the unemployment rate held steady at 6.5%
Canada's services economy contracted for a fifth straight month in October as trade uncertainty and rising prices weighed on activity, S&P Global's Canada services PMI data showed
rose 8.8% after its third-quarter net earnings rose sharply year-over-year on investment gains
slipped 11.5% after a weaker full-year forecast and a narrow quarterly miss
